questions.question: What is an ecosystem? Name three living and three non-living things that could be in one.
questions.expected_answer: An ecosystem is an area where living and non-living things interact and depend on each other. Living things include plants, animals, fungi and bacteria, such as reeds, frogs and fish. Non-living things include sunlight, air, water, soil, rocks and temperature.

questions.question: Describe one water ecosystem and one land ecosystem in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Example of a water ecosystem: a wetland like Nylsvley is land soaked or covered with shallow water for part of the year, with reeds, sedges, frogs, insects and water birds such as herons and storks; it cleans and stores water. Example of a land ecosystem: the Free State grassland has summer rain and cold, dry winters, so grasses grow but few trees, and grazing animals like springbok and blesbok live there.

questions.question: Why is a pond an ecosystem, and how is an ecosystem different from a habitat?
questions.expected_answer: A pond is an ecosystem because inside it living things, like water plants, frogs, fish and insects, and non-living things, like water, sunlight, air and mud, interact and depend on each other. A habitat is only the place where one kind of plant or animal lives, while an ecosystem includes all the living and non-living things in an area and how they work together.
